title: HearAllAges – Hearing Care and Life Situation of People with Hearing loss across All Age groups
summary:
Hearing loss can occur at any age and can affect   various areas of life. HearAllAges investigates how people across all age groups with hearing loss are currently cared for and how they experience their everyday lives. In addition, the project aims to identify areas for improvement in hearing care and  early detection of hearing loss.
The study combines analyses of claims  data with survey data from people with and without diagnosed   hearing loss about their experiences in everyday life and in their interactions with the healthcare system. For the group of children and adolescents, experts are interviewed regarding undetected or late-detected cases.
As part of the project, an online platform on the topic of hearing loss will be developed, which will present the results of the study in an accessible and comprehensive way. By doing so, the scientific findings will be made available to everyone.
conditions: Presence of otological and audiological implants

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of claims data from a German statutory health insurance covering people with hearing loss of all ages (without linkage)
Analysis of claims data from statutory health insurance and the German pension insurance linked with survey data from working-age individuals with hearing loss in the observation period
Retrospective analysis of claims data from the German pension insurance for working-age individuals with hearing loss (without linkage)
Qualitative and quantitative analysis of survey data from individuals with hearing loss across all age groups
Qualitative analysis of interviews with experts experienced in working with children and adolescents with undetected or late-detected hearing loss

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Arm 1: This arm includes individuals who meet the criteria of the case definition in the claims data. Insured persons from all age groups are included. The persons must be covered by the health insurance for at least one day in each quarter of the year. In the case of a newborn child within a year, the insured person must be insured for at least one day in each quarter, starting from the quarter in which the first insurance period began. In the case of death within a year, the insured person must be covered for at least one day in each quarter up to the date of death. The individuals in Arm 1 will be compared with all insured persons. 

Arm 2: This arm includes a sample of statutory health insurance (SHI) insured persons who are employed, of working age, or who were employed in the period of analysis . In addition, the insured persons must have given their written consent to the linked analysis. Three different groups are included: (1) persons with a valid hearing loss diagnosis and hearing aid provision, (2) persons with a valid hearing loss diagnosis without hearing aid provision, and (3) persons without a valid hearing loss diagnosis and without hearing aid provision.

Arm 3: All insured persons who have been documented with a hearing loss diagnosis in the context of a rehabilitation service at the German Pension Insurance are included. The individuals in Arm 3 will be compared with all insured persons.

Arm 4: The survey includes a sample of SHI-insured persons across all age groups. In addition, the insured persons must have given their consent to this analysis. Three different groups are included: (1) persons with a valid hearing loss diagnosis and hearing aid provision, (2) persons with a valid hearing loss diagnosis without hearing aid provision, and (3) persons without a valid hearing loss diagnosis and without hearing aid provision.

Arm 5: In this study arm, experts are interviewed who have experience with children and adolescents whose hearing loss remained undetected for a long time through their profession.
Exclusion criteria:
Arm 1: Insured individuals with implausible sex or age information will be excluded.  Insured individuals who do not meet the criteria of the case definition will be excluded, except for comparative analysis.

Arm 2: All individuals who have not provided consent for data transfer and linkage, or who are not included in the sampling will be excluded. In addition, individuals who are not of working age, or who cannot be assigned to one of the groups will be excluded.

Arm 3: Insured individuals without a documented hearing loss diagnosis in the context of rehabilitation services at the German Pension Insurance will be excluded, except for comparative analysis.

Arm 4: Individuals who were not insured at the participating SHI company, and who cannot be assigned to any of the three groups will be excluded. Furthermore, individuals who did not provide consent for analysis will be excluded.

Arm 5: Individuals who did not provide consent to participate in the interview will be excluded.
